To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Obesity is a chronic inflammatory disease; (2) Inflammation and macrophage related genes are dramatically up-regulated in adipose tissue in obese mice; (3) Macrophages in adipose tissue play an active role; (4) Obesity related insulin resistance is a chronic inflammatory disorder initiated in adipose.
obesity induced insulin resistance is a chronic inflammatory disease.
obesity induced chronic inflammation in adipose tissue is an important factor in the development of insulin resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel molecular targets and therapeutic strategies to treat obesity induced insulin resistance and diabetes.
the role of inflammation in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance and type II diabetes.
understanding the role of macrophage related inflammation in obesity induced insulin resistance and the underlying mechanisms of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
macrophage infiltration and inflammation in WAT is a major contributing factor in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance in obesity.
obesity related insulin sensitivity is an inflammation related disease.
obesity related insulin resistant is, at least, a chronic inflammation disease initiated in fat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity induced inflammation in fat is a key factor in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance and that the insulin sensitizer, rosiglitazones, can reverse this inflammatory state in WAT.
obesity related insulin resistant is a chronic inflammatory disease.
macrophage originated inflammatory genes are up-regulated in WAT of obese mouse models and that this up-regulation precedes the increase of insulin resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity induced inflammation is a cause, not a consequence, of insulin resistance.
macrophages play an important role in obesity induced insulin resistance, a major risk factor for type II diabetes and metabolic syndrome.
obesity is an inflammatory disease, and the inflammation is caused by the macrophages in the fat tissue.
